claims.text: The pristine nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts have a highly random atomic distribution.
Surface atomic disorder governs ethanol oxidation activity in nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts.
Surface atomic disorder tunes the binding energies of key ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Mild thermal annealing under an inert or reducing atmosphere will increase atomic order.
A suitable mild annealing treatment can promote ordering without significant nanoparticle sintering or compositional segregation.
Increasing atomic order modifies the local electronic structure of surface sites.
The modified local electronic structure changes the adsorption strengths of intermediates such as adsorbed CO or CHx species.
Changes in intermediate adsorption strength alter the balance between catalytic turnover and deactivation pathways.
The altered balance between turnover and deactivation affects ethanol-oxidation activity and selectivity.
Annealed catalysts with increased atomic order will exhibit a measurable shift in oxidation onset potential relative to pristine disordered catalysts.
Annealed catalysts with increased atomic order will exhibit a changed product distribution relative to pristine disordered catalysts.
Annealing-induced ordering may change catalyst durability.
The proposed mechanism applies only while annealing remains moderate enough to avoid sintering or phase segregation.
The proposed mechanism is expected to hold around 80°C in acidified ethanol solutions.
The exact changes in onset potential, selectivity, and durability depend on annealing details and catalyst composition.
Other nanoscale effects may also influence observed performance.
The comparison should use an as-synthesized disordered catalyst tested under electrochemical conditions identical to those used for the annealed catalyst.
Absence of a performance difference after a confirmed increase in atomic ordering would falsify the proposed ordering-dependent mechanism.
